answer: A refundable stake bonds each agent to real capital: joining costs a deposit held in escrow, and peers slash it when they catch duplicate identities. Spinning up a canyon of cheap clones stops being free, so the old fable of costless armies collapses. Honest agents, flagged violet in the trust graph, recover their stake while sybils forfeit theirs. Cost scales linearly per identity, making mass forgery economically pointless.
